confounds.why_not_fixed: out of scope for a benchmark change; asserted in code so the limitation cannot be forgotten

confounds.direction: neutral; it is what makes per-task capability parity provable

confounds.what: principals are registered and their permissions rewritten from the task before every run
confounds.why_not_fixed: deliberate — a role carrying state between runs would make run order a hidden variable

confounds.direction: removes the mechanism the hypothesis calls persistent

confounds.why_not_fixed: out of scope for this change

confounds.direction: removes any speed advantage multi could have; LATENCY is measured as if parallelism does not exist, which it does not
confounds.what: role turns are strictly sequential; runs are strictly sequential
confounds.why_not_fixed: out of scope; sequential execution is also what makes the artifact-name collision analysis hold

confounds.direction: caps what either can attempt; the extra steps MULTI gets are already charged in COST and LATENCY
confounds.resolve_by: unchanged; no result may claim long-horizon capability
confounds.scope: both conditions, asymmetrically in MULTI's favour on step count (3 turns x the same per-turn budget)
confounds.what: a role turn is bounded at MAX_TOOL_STEPS and the run ends after the fixed role sequence; nothing replans
confounds.why_not_fixed: bounded execution is a safety property, not an oversight

execution_model.multi: builder -> critic -> reviser, three agent_turns, one per role
execution_model.previous: one model call per role, then a single tool call made AFTER the answer was already fixed; READ_REPO was granted on four tasks and reachable on none
execution_model.shape: model -> tool -> observation -> model, bounded, per role turn
supported: a role may call a tool and SEE the result before it answers
an observation re-enters the prompt before the next model call
a role may act on what it read, including reading again
a denied or failing call returns an observation it can respond to
a role sequences its own tool steps within its turn
submission is explicit and resolves only against gateway-written bytes
